title: ECO-CHIP: Estimation of Carbon Footprint of Chiplet-based Architectures for Sustainable VLSI
problem: Existing embodied carbon analysis tools are designed for monolithic chip architectures and do not apply to heterogeneous integration (HI) chiplet-based systems. There is no methodology to assess embodied carbon emissions (from design, manufacturing, and packaging) for chiplet-based designs accounting for yields, reuse patterns, and packaging complexity.
motivation: Embodied carbon emissions have become a critical concern in semiconductor manufacturing as operational power efficiency improves, making it essential to optimize chiplet reuse and heterogeneous integration strategies for sustainable computing.
method: ECO-CHIP models embodied carbon footprint by accounting for chiplet scaling, chip yields, packaging yields, design complexity, and advanced packaging overheads. The tool is integrated with chiplet simulators to jointly analyze carbon, power, area, and cost across different chiplet disaggregation scenarios and design generations.
key_novelty: First carbon footprint estimation tool designed specifically for heterogeneous integration systems that quantifies the embodied carbon benefits of chiplet IP reuse across multiple designs and IC generations.
contributions: ECO-CHIP tool for embodied carbon assessment of chiplet-based heterogeneous integration architectures
Evidence that HI systems achieve up to 30% embodied carbon reduction versus monolithic designs
Comprehensive modeling framework for yields, packaging complexity, and design reuse effects on carbon
Integration with chiplet simulators enabling joint carbon-power-area-cost optimization

metrics.other: embodied carbon reduction up to 30% versus monolithic systems; power, area, and cost jointly analyzed
